quarter.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New the third quarter. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.8pt">The U.S. year-over-year net rooms growth rate continued to improve, with U.S. rooms approximately flat compared to September 30, 2025, as third-quarter room exits declined 23% compared to the same period of 2025. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.98pt">Global net rooms grew 1.7% compared to September 30, 2025, led by 2.5% growth across the higher-revenue extended stay, midscale, and upscale brands.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.8pt">U.S. RevPAR increased 3.8% in the third quarter compared to the same period of 2025, reflecting improvements in both occupancy and rate.</font></div><div style="text-indent:18pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font compared to the same period of 2025, representing 6,900 new rooms for development. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.98pt">The U.S. conversion pipeline grew to 25,500 rooms, an increase of 6% from June 30, 2026, and 29% from September 30, 2025, driving sequential growth in the total U.S. pipeline.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font quarter compared to the same period of 2025.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font hotels for estimated net cash proceeds of approximately $34 million, while retaining franchise agreements for both properties.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.98pt">Net income was $58 million for the third quarter, a 68% decline compared to the same period of 2025. The decline primarily reflected a $100 million gain from the acquisition of a joint venture recognized in the prior-year quarter. Current-year results included a $24 million charge related to the termination of an arrangement involving an option to acquire a European hospitality business operating primarily under a lease-based model and a $6 million non-cash impairment charge related to two owned hotels. These impacts were partially offset by higher franchise and management fees. The prior-year gain and both current-year charges are excluded from adjusted results.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%;padding-left:13.98pt">Adjusted EBITDA increased 1% to $193 million for the third quarter compared to the same period of 2025, primarily driven by higher U.S. royalties, partially offset by lower liquidated damages revenue and higher adjusted SG&#38;A expenses. Excluding liquidated damages revenue of $3.3 million and $9.5 million in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively, adjusted EBITDA increased 5% compared to the same period of 2025. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.98pt">Adjusted diluted EPS increased 11% for the third quarter</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">compared to the same period of 2025, benefiting from higher franchise and management fees and share repurchases. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:36pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:13.98pt">Franchise and management fees increased 5% to $204 million for the third quarter compared to the same period of 2025, primarily reflecting higher U.S. royalties driven by RevPAR growth </font></div><div style="border-bottom:1pt solid #000000;margin-bottom:5pt;margin-top:10pt;opacity:1;width:150pt"></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Calculated as total revenues excluding reimbursable revenues. Reimbursable revenues totaled $173 million and $169 million for third quarter 2026 and 2025, respectively, and $460 million and $460 million for each of the nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. Excluding liquidated damages revenue of $3.3 million and $9.5 million in the third quarters of 2026 and 2025, respectively, revenues excluding reimbursable revenues increased 5% in the third quarter compared to the same period of 2025.</font></div><div style="height:42.75pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr The Company's net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA ratio was 3.2x for the trailing twelve months ended September 30, 2026, within its target range of 3.0x to 4.0x. The quarter-end cash balance included borrowings made in advance of the October 1, 2026, acquisition of Harvest Hosts. Following the acquisition, net leverage remained within the Company's target range.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In August 2026, the Company completed a $500 million unsecured term loan financing, reducing the borrowing spread on the refinanced debt by 15 basis points and increasing available capacity under its $1 billion revolving credit facility. The term loan matures in August 2029.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company generated $122 million in cash flows from operating activities, compared to $185 million in the prior-year period. The decrease primarily reflected the contract termination payment, higher franchise agreement acquisition costs associated with a 17% increase in U.S. room openings, and higher marketing and reservation system reimbursable expenses, partially offset by deferred tax and working capital timing effects. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:115%;text-decoration:underline">Asset Recycling</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:115%">During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net capital outlays for hotel development and lending activities declined 56% to $36.3 million, compared to $82.0 million in the prior-year period.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.47pt;font-weight:400;line-height:115%;position:relative;top:-4.02pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">The Company advanced its return to an asset-light franchising model through sales from its owned hotel portfolio. Subsequent to quarter-end, the Company sold two owned hotels, generating estimated net cash proceeds of approximately $34 million while retaining franchise agreements for both properties. As of November 2, 2026, the Company owned 17 operating hotels, with one additional hotel under construction. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:115%;text-decoration:underline">Acquisition</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:115%">On October 1, 2026, the Company acquired Harvest Hosts, an asset-light RV travel subscription platform with recurring revenue, expanding Choice Hotels&#8217; offerings for value-minded travelers into the outdoor travel market. The approximately $130 million transaction was funded with available cash and borrowings under the Company&#8217;s revolving credit facility.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:115%;text-decoration:underline">Shareholder Returns</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font through dividends and $172 million in share repurchases.</font><font The revised adjusted SG&#38;A outlook, excluding Harvest Host, reflects primarily non-recurring spending on certain strategic initiatives and artificial intelligence-enabled capabilities, as well as higher accounts receivable reserves.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">Net capital outlays for hotel development-related activities are expected to decline from $103.4 million in 2025 to approximately $20 million in 2026, assuming no additional hotel sales.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.47pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%;position:relative;top:-4.02pt;vertical-align:baseline">2</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="height:42.75pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:42.75pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">Webcast and Conference Call</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">Choice will host a conference call to discuss third quarter 2026 results on November 2, 2026, at 10&#58;00 a.m. ET. A wide-ranging portfolio of 22 brands that includes full-service upper upscale, midscale, extended stay, and economy properties enables Choice&#174; to meet travelers&#8217; needs in more places and for more occasions while driving more value for franchise owners and shareholders. The award-winning Choice Privileges&#174; rewards program and co-brand credit card options provide members with a fast and easy way to earn reward nights and personalized perks. We undertake no obligation to publicly update or revise any forward-looking statement, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise, except as required by law.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%;text-decoration:underline">Non-GAAP Financial Measurements and Other Definitions</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">The company evaluates its operations utilizing the performance metrics of adjusted EBITDA, adjusted selling, general and administrative (SG&#38;A) expenses, adjusted net income, and adjusted diluted EPS, which are all non-GAAP financial measurements. These measures, which are reconciled to the comparable GAAP measures in Exhibits 6 and 7, should not be considered as an alternative to any measure of performance or liquidity as promulgated under or authorized by GAAP, such as SG&#38;A, net income and EPS. The company&#8217;s calculation of these measurements may be different from the calculations used by other companies and comparability may therefore be limited. Management believes these non-GAAP financial measures provide investors with additional meaningful financial information that should be considered when assessing our underlying business performance and trends. We further discuss management&#8217;s reasons for reporting these non-GAAP measures and how each non-GAAP measure is calculated below.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%"> </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">In addition to the specific adjustments noted below with respect to each measure, the non-GAAP measures presented herein also exclude restructuring of the company&#8217;s operations including employee severance benefit, contract termination costs, legal costs, acquisition related to business combination, due diligence and transition (recoveries) costs, and global ERP system implementation and related costs to allow for period-over-period comparison of ongoing core operations before the impact of these discrete and infrequent charges.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">The non-GAAP measures presented herein also include certain information regarding projected non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA contributions from the estimated benefit from the Harvest Host acquisition, which we are unable to reconcile to similar projections of net income without unreasonable efforts as the adjustments cannot reasonably be predicted. The impact of the unavailable information could be significant relative to our expectations.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%">Adjusted Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization&#58;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%"> Adjusted EBITDA, presented herein, is calculated as net income excluding the impact of interest expense, interest income, provision for income taxes, depreciation and amortization, amortization of cloud computing </font></div><div style="height:42.75pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:42.75pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">arrangements, impairments and gains on sale of business, joint ventures and assets, other (gains) and losses, equity in net income (loss) of unconsolidated affiliates and (gain) loss on extinguishment of debt, further adjusted to exclude certain items, including, franchisee agreement acquisition cost amortization and charges, mark-to-market adjustments on non-qualified retirement plan investments, share based compensation expense (benefit) and surplus or deficits generated by reimbursable revenue from franchised and managed properties. We consider adjusted EBITDA to be an indicator of operating performance because it measures our ability to service debt, fund capital expenditures, and expand our business. We also use these measures, as do analysts, lenders, investors, and others, to evaluate companies because they exclude certain items that can vary widely across industries or among companies within the same industry. For example, interest expense can be dependent on a company&#8217;s capital structure, debt levels, and credit ratings, and share based compensation expense (benefit) is dependent on the design of compensation plans in place and the usage of them. Accordingly, the impact of interest expense and share based compensation expense (benefit) on earnings can vary significantly among companies. The tax positions of companies can also vary because of their differing abilities to take advantage of tax benefits and because of the tax policies of the jurisdictions in which they operate. As a result, effective tax rates and provision for income taxes can vary considerably among companies. These measures also exclude depreciation and amortization because companies utilize productive assets of different ages and use different methods of both acquiring and depreciating productive assets or amortizing franchise-agreement acquisition costs. These differences can result in considerable variability in the relative asset costs and estimated lives and, therefore, the depreciation and amortization expense among companies. Mark-to-market adjustments on non-qualified retirement-plan investments recorded in SG&#38;A expenses are excluded from adjusted EBITDA, as the company accounts for these investments in accordance with accounting for deferred-compensation arrangements when investments are held in a rabbi trust and invested. Changes in the fair value of the investments are recognized as both compensation expense in SG&#38;A and other gains and losses. As a result, the changes in the fair value of the investments do not have a material impact on the company&#8217;s net income. Surpluses and deficits generated from reimbursable revenues from franchised and managed properties are excluded, as the company does not operate these programs to generate a profit and has the contractual rights to adjust future collections or assess additional fees to recover prior period expenditures. The company&#8217;s franchise and management agreements require these revenues to be used exclusively for expenses associated with providing franchise and management services, such as central reservation systems, hotel employee and operating costs, reservation delivery and national marketing and media advertising. Franchised and managed property owners are required to reimburse the company for any deficits generated from these activities and the company is required to spend any surpluses generated in future periods. The reimbursement for franchise and management services is typically billed and collected monthly, based on the underlying hotel&#8217;s sales or usage, while the associated costs are recognized as incurred by the company, creating timing differences with the net effect impacting net income in the reporting period. These timing differences are due to our discretion to spend in excess of the revenues earned or less than the revenues earned in a single period to ensure that the programs are operated in the best long-term interests of our franchised and managed properties. Since these activities will be managed to break-even over time, quarterly or annual surpluses and deficits have been excluded from the measurements utilized to assess the company&#8217;s operating performance.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%">Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share&#58;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%"> Adjusted net income and adjusted diluted EPS exclude the impact of surpluses or deficits generated from reimbursable revenue from franchised and managed properties, impairments, formation costs and gains on sale of business, joint ventures and assets and gains on extinguishment of debt. Surpluses and deficits generated from reimbursable revenue from franchised and managed properties are excluded, as the company does not operate these programs to generate a profit and has the contractual rights to adjust future collections or assess additional fees to recover prior period expenditures. The company&#8217;s franchise agreements require these revenues to be used exclusively for expenses associated with providing franchised and managed services, such as central reservation systems, </font></div><div style="height:42.75pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:42.75pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">hotel employee and operating costs, reservation delivery and national marketing and media advertising. Franchised and managed property owners are required to reimburse the company for any deficits generated from activities and the company is required to spend any surpluses generated in future periods. The reimbursement for franchise and management services is typically billed and collected monthly, based on the underlying hotel&#8217;s sales or usage, while the associated costs are recognized as incurred by the company, creating timing differences with the net effect impacting net income in the reporting period. These timing differences are due to our discretion to spend in excess of the revenues earned or less than the revenues earned in a single period to ensure that the programs are operated in the best long-term interests of our franchised and managed properties. Since these activities will be managed to break-even over time, quarterly or annual surpluses and deficits have been excluded from the measurements utilized to assess the company&#8217;s operating performance. We consider adjusted net income and adjusted diluted EPS to be indicators of operating performance because excluding these items allows for period-over-period comparisons of our ongoing operations.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%">Adjusted SG&#38;A&#58;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%"> Adjusted SG&#38;A reflects SG&#38;A excluding the impact of mark-to-market adjustments on non-qualified retirement plan investments, amortization of cloud computing arrangements and share based compensation expense. We use this measure, as do analysts, lenders, investors, and others, to evaluate companies because it excludes certain items that can vary widely across industries or among companies within the same industry. For example, share based compensation expense (benefit) is dependent on the design of compensation plans in place and the usage of them. Accordingly, the impact of share-based compensation expense (benefit) on earnings can vary significantly among companies. Mark-to-market adjustments on non-qualified retirement-plan investments recorded in SG&#38;A expenses are also excluded as the company accounts for these investments in accordance with accounting for deferred-compensation arrangements when investments are held in a rabbi trust and invested. Changes in the fair value of the investments are recognized as both compensation expense in SG&#38;A and other gains and losses. As a result, the changes in the fair value of the investments do not have a material impact on the company&#8217;s net income.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%">Occupancy&#58;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%"> Occupancy represents the total number of room nights sold divided by the total number of room nights available at a hotel for a given period. Occupancy measures the utilization of the hotels&#8217; available capacity. Management uses occupancy to gauge demand at a specific hotel or group of hotels in a given period. The company calculates occupancy based on information as reported by its franchisees. To accurately reflect occupancy, the company may revise its prior years&#8217; operating statistics for the most current information provided.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%">Average Daily Rate (ADR)&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">ADR represents hotel room revenue divided by the total number of room nights sold for a given period. ADR measures the average room price attained by a hotel and ADR trends provide useful information concerning the pricing environment and the nature of the customer base of a hotel or group of hotels. ADR is a commonly used performance measure in the industry, and management uses ADR to assess pricing levels that the company is able to generate. The company calculates ADR based on information as reported by its franchisees. To accurately reflect ADR, the company may revise its prior years&#8217; operating statistics for the most current information provided. </font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%">Revenue Per Available Room</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%"> (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%">RevPAR)&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">RevPAR is calculated by dividing hotel room revenue by the total number of room nights available to guests for a given period. Management considers RevPAR to be a meaningful indicator of hotel performance and therefore company royalty and system revenues as it provides a metric correlated to the two key drivers of operations at a hotel&#58; occupancy and ADR. The company calculates RevPAR based on information as reported by its franchisees. To accurately reflect RevPAR, the company may revise its prior years&#8217; operating statistics for the most current information provided. RevPAR is also a useful indicator in measuring performance over comparable periods.</font></div><div style="height:42.75pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:42.75pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:112%">Pipeline&#58; </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">Pipeline is defined as hotels awaiting conversion, under construction or approved for development, and master development agreements committing owners to future franchise development.</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%"> </font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline">Contacts</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Allie Summers, Senior Director, Investor Relations</font></div><div><font style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">IR&#64;choicehotels.com</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#169; 2026 Choice Hotels International, Inc. All rights reserved.</font></div><div style="height:42.75pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><div id="i512aea8276b442688bf4cbc7b4e7d086_7"></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:42.75pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="text-align:center"><font
